entry.title: Accuracy of Advertising and Notice of Insured Status (NCUA credit union advertising rule)
entry.summary: Accuracy of Advertising and Notice of Insured Status Federal Register · Nov 16, 2026 · Rule · Effective Dec 16, 2026The National Credit Union Administration issued a final rule streamlining its regulations on advertising and notice of insured status. It removes provisions concerning the official advertising statement to reduce administrative burden and give federally insured credit unions more flexibility. The rule does not amend requirements for displaying the official sign and takes effect December 16, 2026. entry.title: CFTC sues Louisiana over state court order shutting down CFTC-regulated exchanges
entry.summary: CFTC Sues Louisiana After State Court Blocks CFTC-Regulated Exchanges CFTC · Nov 13, 2026 · EnforcementThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Louisiana to block the state from banning event contracts offered by CFTC-regulated exchanges, clearing organizations and futures commission merchants. A state court had ordered more than 30 companies in the state to stop operating without notice or a chance to be heard. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said event contracts have traded openly in Louisiana for years and that the suit seeks to preserve the status quo while federal courts decide the issue.

entry.title: IRS names 10 new members to the Electronic Tax Administration Advisory Committee
entry.summary: IRS appoints 10 new members to Electronic Tax Administration Advisory Committee IRS · Nov 13, 2026 · PersonnelThe IRS announced the appointment of 10 new members to the Electronic Tax Administration Advisory Committee (ETAAC). Established by statute in 1998, the committee is a public forum for discussing electronic tax administration issues. Its members include state tax officials, cybersecurity experts, tax professionals, software developers, and representatives from payroll, financial, and consumer groups.

entry.title: IRS fiscal 2026 results: record tax collections, faster refunds and expanded digital services
entry.summary: IRS achieved historic performance in 2026 for American taxpayers, efficiently delivering new tax benefits to working families IRS · Oct 29, 2026 · ReportThe IRS announced its fiscal year 2026 results, reporting record tax collections of $5.6 trillion, up nearly 5 percent from the previous year. Total refunds and average refunds both increased, with about 90 percent of electronic filers receiving refunds in less than 21 days. The release also covers growth in digital service use, about $38 billion in revenue protected from identity theft refund fraud, and progress on Trump Accounts for children. Correction Nov 14, 2026: Publication date changed from Oct 30, 2026 to Oct 29, 2026

entry.title: CFTC sues Arkansas to defend federal jurisdiction over prediction markets
entry.summary: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets CFTC · Nov 13, 2026 · EnforcementOn November 13, 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) announced a lawsuit against Arkansas to block the state's effort to halt event-contract trading and impose civil penalties on CFTC-registered exchanges. The CFTC says Arkansas's civil enforcement action against Kalshi in state court is preempted by federal law. Chairman Michael S. Selig said the agency will keep defending its sole jurisdiction under the Commodity Exchange Act. Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued.

entry.title: SEC proposes reforms to executive and director pay disclosure rules
entry.summary: SEC Proposes Executive and Director Compensation Disclosure Reforms SEC · Nov 14, 2026 · Draft / consultationOn November 13, 2026, the SEC proposed amendments to Item 402 of Regulation S-K to make executive and director compensation disclosure more principles-based and materiality-driven. The proposal would focus named executive officer disclosure on the principal executive and financial officers, replace four tables with three new ones, raise the perquisites reporting threshold to $150,000, and simplify pay-versus-performance and pay ratio requirements. Public comments are accepted for 60 days after Federal Register publication. The archived text and attachments run to about 1,207,539 characters; the summary is based only on the first 12,000. entry.title: NYSE Arca Proposes Moving Franklin Responsibly Sourced Gold ETF to Generic Listing Standards
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Arca, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Franklin Responsibly Sourced Gold ETF Federal Register · Nov 13, 2026 · CryptoTopic evidence: 「Rule 8.201–E (Generic), as amended, allows for up to 15% of a trust’s net asset value (NAV) to consist of digital commodities or securities that do not independently meet the core generic eligibility 」 NYSE Arca has filed a rule change to shift the Franklin Responsibly Sourced Gold ETF's listing basis from Rule 8.201–E (Non-Generic) to Rule 8.201–E (Generic). The amended generic rule, approved in July 2026, allows up to 15% of a trust's NAV to consist of digital commodities. The Exchange states the Shares will meet the amended generic rule's initial and continued listing requirements. The change took effect on filing, and comments are due by December 4, 2026. entry.title: National Television Multiple Ownership Rule
entry.summary: National Television Multiple Ownership Rule Federal Register · Nov 12, 2026 · Rule · Effective Jan 11, 2027The FCC repeals the national television multiple ownership rule, which barred commercial TV licensees from holding cognizable interests in stations with an aggregate national audience reach above 39%. Under the new approach, proposed transactions that would have been barred will be reviewed case by case to determine whether they serve the goals of localism, viewpoint diversity, and competition.. entry.title: IRS reminder: Permanent deduction for charitable gifts by non-itemizers starts with returns filed next year
entry.summary: IRS reminder: Permanent charitable contribution deduction begins for returns filed next year for taxpayers who do not itemize IRS · Nov 10, 2026 · GuidanceThe IRS reminded taxpayers who take the standard deduction that the Working Families Tax Cuts law makes permanent a deduction for charitable contributions starting in 2026. Eligible cash gifts to qualified charities can be deducted up to $1,000, or $2,000 for married couples filing jointly. Noncash gifts, contributions to supporting organizations, and donor advised funds do not qualify, and donors should keep records of their gifts.

entry.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals Who Acted as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
entry.summary: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers CFTC · Nov 9, 2026 · EnforcementThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued orders against eight individuals for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. The brokers solicited off-exchange leveraged or margined retail forex and commodity transactions from U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants, without the respondents registering as required. The orders require the respondents to cease the conduct, bar them for two years from registering with the Commission or acting for any CFTC registrant, and recognize penalties owed in a related SEC proceeding.

entry.title: Withdrawal of Proposal to Lower Cross-Border Funds Transfer Information Threshold and Clarify Crypto Application
entry.summary: Threshold for the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Funds Transfers and Transmittals of Funds That Begin or End Outside the United States, and Clarification of the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currencies and Digital Assets With Legal Tender Status; Withdrawal Federal Register · Nov 9, 2026 · Draft / consultation · CryptoTopic evidence: 「Clarification of the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currencies and Digital Assets With Legal Tender Status」 FinCEN and the Federal Reserve Board are withdrawing a 2020 joint proposal that would have lowered the threshold for collecting and transmitting information on cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and clarified that the rules apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency and digital assets with legal tender status. The agencies cite the passage of more than five years since the proposal and significant recent developments in the crypto industry. Any future amendments would be considered in light of these changes and subject to further public comment.
